vendor.blurb: Kling once topped the AA video board; now behind Seedance and Wan, eyeing 4.0 in October

highlights: Native 30-second generation, up to 10 keyframes of control
Up to 4K output and 10-bit HDR, with 21:9 support
Omni Reference accepts up to 15 multimodal references
Dual-channel stereo, tighter lip-sync, multiple languages and dialects
kling-4.0.notes: Announced 9/28; full release in October, currently in closed beta. Cello, an anonymous entry on AA, is suspected to be this model. No public leaderboard results yet; the tier is provisional.

kling-4.0-flash.tagline: Fast early cut of 4.0, Ultra annual plans only
highlights: Open to Ultra annual subscribers from 9/28 (top China plan from ¥916/month)
Faster and cheaper than the full 4.0
Early users praise its prompt understanding
kling-4.0-flash.notes: No leaderboard results yet; tier B is provisional, following the usual lightweight-model convention.

kling-3.0.tagline: February's #1 on the AA text-to-video board
highlights: Ranked #1 on AA text-to-video (with and without audio) at launch
Standard 720p and Pro 1080p tiers, plus an Omni version
kling-3.0.notes: Kling 3.0 Omni (multi-reference and editing) is folded in here; its AA text-to-video score is 1075-1082.

kling-image-3.0.tagline: The image model that makes Kling's first frames
highlights: Launched the same day as Video 3.0, plus an Image 3.0 Omni
Native 2K/4K output with visual chain-of-thought reasoning
Built to give video generation consistent characters and first frames
kling-image-3.0.notes: Not in the top 30 of LMArena or AA image boards. Its predecessor Kolors has largely left the mainstream and isn't listed. Kling Image 4.0 has leaked but isn't out.
